name: Viking 1
summary: The first U.S. lander to work successfully on Mars, photographing the surface and testing soil for signs of life until a faulty command ended contact.
discoveries: Sent back pictures and weather data from Mars for about six years.
Ran experiments on Martian soil to look for signs of life.

stories.kids: I was the first U.S. lander to work successfully on Mars, and I kept going for years. I scooped up soil and tested it for tiny living things. In 1982 a mistaken command from Earth cut off my signal, but my pictures changed how we see Mars.
stories.explorer: Viking 1 touched down on Chryse Planitia on July 20, 1976 and operated until November 11, 1982, when a faulty command sent from Earth interrupted communications. NASA spent months trying, without success, to regain contact.
stories.scientist: Viking Lander 1 landed in western Chryse Planitia on July 20, 1976. Communications were lost in November 1982 after a faulty command; JPL attempts to re-establish contact were unsuccessful. The lander was renamed the Thomas A. Mutch Memorial Station.

timeline.text: Viking 1 lands, then photographs the surface and tests the soil for signs of life.

timeline.title: The signal fades
timeline.text: A faulty command from Earth interrupts communications. NASA keeps trying, without success.

learn.title: Who I am
learn.text: I’m Viking 1. I landed in Chryse Planitia on July 20, 1976, and I was the first U.S. lander to work successfully on Mars, and I kept going for years, not days.

learn.title: What I did
learn.text: I photographed the surface, sent back weather data, and ran biology experiments to test Martian soil for signs of life.

learn.title: How it ended
learn.text: On November 11, 1982, a faulty command sent from Earth interrupted my communications. NASA tried for months, without success.
